chunks: And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: A man married a young virgin bondwoman on the condition that he would not deflower her, then afterward she gave him permission.
He عليه السلام said: If she gave him permission, then there is no harm in it.

key_terms.بِجَارِيَةٍ: with a bondwoman or female slave
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or legal objection
key_terms.لَا يَقْتَضَّهَا: that he would not deflower her

ai.seo_question: If a man marries with the condition that he will not deflower the woman, can he do so later if she permits it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a marriage contract involving a young virgin bondwoman where a condition was made not to deflower her. The Imam عليه السلام states that if she later grants permission, then there is no objection, indicating the ruling turns on her subsequent consent.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4612 - It is narrated from Ishaq in Ammar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (as): A man married a young bondwoman with the condition that he would not deflower her. Then afterward, she gave him permission.
Imam (as) replied: "If she gave him permission, then there is no harm in it."
